title: Replace the triple lock with a smoothed earnings link
headline: Replace the triple lock with a smoothed earnings link: RF, saves £0.65bn by 2029-30.
description: The Resolution Foundation’s alternative to the triple lock: uprate the state pension with earnings, smoothed so that a temporary burst of inflation does not cut its real value, and no 2.5% floor. RF puts the net saving at around £650 million in 2029-30, after the extra means-tested benefits and lower income tax that follow, and growing every year after. It leaves the basic state pension at £199.65 a week in 2029-30 against £200.95 under the triple lock. A different design from uprating by prices alone, and a smaller saving; breaking the manifesto promise all the same.

baselinePolicy.text: The triple lock raises the state pension by the highest of CPI inflation, average earnings growth and 2.5%; on the OBR’s forecast the 2.5% floor binds from 2027-28.

terms.label: The Resolution Foundation’s net saving from a smoothed earnings link in place of the triple lock from 2027-28, as a saving
terms.unit: £ million, 2029-30, net of means-tested benefits and income tax

source.quote: This would save around £650 million in 2029-30 (net of increased spending on means-tested benefits and lower income tax receipts)

rawSource.note: RF’s 2029-30 net saving held flat in cash from the start year, entered as a negative spending effect. RF says the saving is smaller before 2029-30 and grows after it. Nobody in government has costed it.

caveats: RF’s figure is net of higher means-tested benefits and lower income tax; the gross saving on the state pension line is larger. Held flat here, although RF says it grows every year and would be smaller in the first years.
The saving depends on the forecast: with earnings growth above 2.5%, a smoothed earnings link and the triple lock pay much the same and the saving shrinks.
Outside the welfare cap, and a manifesto promise: the government has committed to the triple lock for this parliament.

considerations.text: RF’s saving comes from dropping the 2.5% floor when earnings grow more slowly than that; a price shock would be smoothed rather than banked, which is the design’s point and also why the saving moves with the forecast.

sources.quote: protects the value of the State Pension from temporary price shocks

considerations.text: Every state pensioner: £1.30 a week less on the basic state pension by 2029-30 on RF’s figures, and more each year after.

sources.quote: £199.65 per week in 2029-30, compared to £200.95 with triple lock uprating

considerations.text: The manifesto promised to keep the triple lock; any replacement breaks it, and the earnings element is in statute, so this needs an Act.

interactions.text: Two replacements for the triple lock. Pick one: prices alone saves more; a smoothed earnings link keeps pensions rising with pay.
